## Natural history notes

A small shining leaf chafer characterized by a rounded, glossy body that is usually tan to brown with a darker margin or subtle greenish-bronze sheen. In Florida, the Margined Shining Leaf Chafer is found in warm wooded and semi-open habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, yards, and areas with shrubs or low vegetation. Adults feed on leaves and may come to lights, while the larvae of related shining leaf chafers live in soil and feed on roots or decaying organic material, helping connect plant growth, soil processes, and insect-eating predators.
